cases.before:
Removed condition sets in the new Release conditions history tab render raw internal IDs instead of human-readable names. To see it, edit a flag's release conditions to delete a condition set that filters on a flag dependency with no stored PropertyFilter `label`, or on a `distinct_id` value, then open that history entry's Release conditions tab.

`FeatureFlagReleaseConditionsChange.tsx:48` constructs `featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic` with `filters: after`, so `filterGroups` only reflects the after-state. `flagIds` and `distinctIds` are derived from `filterGroups` ([`featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic.ts:1121-1148`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/66b1c1750c57b7040cbb0a179d96f60e02e16853/frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic.ts#L1121-L1148)), so an id that appears only in `before` is left out of both name-resolution lists. `afterMount` loads flag keys and distinct-id names for exactly those two lists ([`featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic.ts:1195-1203`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/66b1c1750c57b7040cbb0a179d96f60e02e16853/frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic.ts#L1195-L1203)), so removed-only ids are never fetched. The 'Removed by this change' cards then call `getFlagKey`/`getDistinctIdName` for their properties, and both return the raw id when nothing was fetched for it ([`featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic.ts:1117`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/66b1c1750c57b7040cbb0a179d96f60e02e16853/frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic.ts#L1117) and [`featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic.ts:1154`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/66b1c1750c57b7040cbb0a179d96f60e02e16853/frontend/src/scenes/feature-flags/featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic.ts#L1154)).

The result is that a removed condition set that targeted a flag dependency without a stored label shows the bare numeric flag id, and one that targeted `distinct_id` always shows the bare distinct id rather than the resolved person name. That is permanent, not just a flash during an async load.

Pass both before and after groups into the logic's filters, e.g. merge `after.groups` and `before?.groups` when constructing `filters`, so name resolution covers removed sets too. A story or test rendering a removed condition set whose properties include a flag-dependency id with no label and a `distinct_id` filter, asserting the removed card shows resolved names and keys rather than raw ids, would cover it.

```diff
        id: `${flagId}-activity-${activityId}`,
        readOnly: true,
-       filters: after,
+       filters: { ...after, groups: [...(after.groups ?? []), ...(before?.groups ?? [])] },
```

Include both before and after groups in the logic's filters:

```

cases.before:
Reopening a previously-viewed history entry's Release conditions tab re-fetches flag keys and distinct-id names it already resolved moments earlier. It shows up when a flag's condition sets reference flag-dependency or `distinct_id` filters and a user expands a history row's Release conditions tab, collapses the row, then reopens it.

`featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic` is keyed per history entry (`${flagId}-activity-${activityId}`), and `flagKeyCache`/`distinctIdNameCache` are reducers on that keyed instance. Collapsing the row unmounts the tab strip, which tears down the keyed logic instance along with its caches. Reopening the row re-mounts the logic with an empty cache, so `afterMount` refetches the same flag keys and distinct-id names.

Each reopen of the same row therefore costs a fresh `bulkKeys`/`getByDistinctIds` round trip (up to two requests per 200 distinct ids), and the reader briefly sees raw ids again. Moving the two caches into a shared, unkeyed logic that survives a row's collapse and reopen would avoid that. No regression test needed here: cache lifetime is a performance characteristic rather than a correctness contract, and checking it would mean asserting on internal Kea state rather than observable behavior.

Move `flagKeyCache`/`distinctIdNameCache` into a shared, unkeyed logic (e.g. `flagLabelCacheLogic`) that survives a row's collapse/reopen, and connect it from `featureFlagReleaseConditionsLogic` instead of keeping the caches local to the per-entry keyed instance.
cases.after:
Collapsing a history row discards its name caches. Reopening it fetches the same flag keys and distinct-id names again and briefly shows raw IDs.

Consider keeping `flagKeyCache` and `distinctIdNameCache` in shared logic that survives the row closing.

It says the rule is about 'two sets at the same position', which matches the third matching pass, where `looksLikeSameSet(group, beforeGroups[afterIndex])` compares two sets at the same index. The fourth pass calls the same function over every unclaimed before-set specifically to catch a set that moved, so those two sets are usually at different positions. The comment also leaves 'target the same type of thing' unexplained.

A reader trusting the comment would believe the position constraint applies everywhere `looksLikeSameSet` is used, including the moved-set pass where it does not, and would still have to read the function body to learn what 'same type of thing' means.

Drop the positional claim and state the actual rule: same aggregation group and overlapping property key, or neither has properties.

-// kind of thing. Without this, removing set 1 and appending an unrelated set would read as an edit.
+// Two sets count as the same set only when they use the same aggregation group and share at least one
+// property key, or neither has properties. Without this, removing set 1 and appending an unrelated

```
